study type: Registry-based cohort study with retrospective data collection
exposure: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) exposure in late pregnancy
Serotonin norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) exposure in late pregnancy
outcome: Estimated blood loss >=500 mL following vaginal delivery
Estimated blood loss >=1,000 mL following cesarean section
cohort: The study included 953 participants from the National Pregnancy Registry for Psychiatric Medications, comprising women with psychiatric illness either exposed (n=500) or unexposed (n=453) to SSRIs/SNRIs proximate to delivery.
finding: SSRI/SNRI exposure in late pregnancy was associated with a modestly increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio 1.33, 95% CI [0.90, 1.97]) compared to no exposure.
mod_finding: When stratified by delivery type, the increased risk of PPH with SSRI/SNRI exposure was particularly evident after C-section delivery (adjusted odds ratio 2.21, 95% CI [1.18, 4.13]) but not significantly after vaginal delivery (odds ratio 1.04, 95% CI [0.63, 1.70]).
